⚠️ The card's What section says `PermissionMatrixEditPage.doSave`. **There is no such file.** `git ls-tree` over the whole tree returns exactly one match for this component: `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/PermissionMatrixEditor.tsx`. Triage's row has the right file; the card body does not. Read at `c1006ed8e`:

| line | reading |
|---|---|
| `:790` | `const lay = await client.layered<PermissionSetDraft>(type, payload.name);` — ⛔ **no `.catch`** |
| `:791` | `resetDraftBaseline(toDisplayDraft((lay.effective ?? toSave) as PermissionSetDraft));` — skipped on a rejection |
| `:793` | `setDestructive(null);` — also skipped |
| ⭐ CONTROL, same file | `:437` — `client.layered<PermissionSetDraft>(type, name).catch(() => null),` |
| second control, same function | `:768` — a `.catch` kept explicitly *"so the rejection can never escape as an unhandled …"* |

⇒ two `.catch`ed `layered` calls and one bare one, in one file. The bare one is the card.

## ⛔ THE FENCE, and it is the whole card

Triage, verbatim: 「要改的是**这一处读回的失败语义**(保存已成,读回失败只该降级显示),⛔ **不是**给该文件所有 `client.layered` 统一加 `.catch` —— `:437` 那处的 `rereadFailed` 是**故意**要拦住写入的。」

⇒ `:437`'s catch **stops a write on purpose**. ⛔ Do not unify the file's `layered` error handling, do not "make them consistent", and ⛔ do not touch `:437` or `:768`. A sweep here would convert a deliberate write-blocking guard into a degraded display — a far worse defect than the one you are fixing, on a permission surface.

## Scope — three consequences, and a fix that closes one of them is not the card

The save has already landed when `:790` rejects. The card names three outcomes and all three are in scope:

1. the red error strip renders the transport's message for a write that **succeeded**;
2. `resetDraftBaseline` never runs ⇒ `isDirty` stays **true**, so the editor keeps claiming unsaved changes and the `beforeunload` guard keeps firing on a persisted record;
3. `setDestructive(null)` is skipped.

⚠️ The card is explicit that the post-save re-read failing should **only degrade the display**. So the save's own outcome must read as success, and the baseline must still be re-anchored from what you have (`toSave` is the fallback the line already spells) rather than left un-anchored. ⛔ If you find a shape where the author cannot be told that the re-read specifically failed without also being told the save failed, **stop and report** — that is a ruling, not a fix.

## ⛔ Hard constraints

- ⛔ **Not objectui#9420, and not PR objectui#9483.** That was the PACKAGE door and a data-loss defect; its ruling *required the whole-record arm to keep behaving exactly as it does today*, which is why this was fenced out. This card is the environment door, and it loses no data.
- ⛔ **Do not change what is saved.** The record on the server is already correct. Only the aftermath of the re-read moves.
- ⛔ objectui `AGENTS.md:316`: never `git push --force` or `--force-with-lease`, never push to `main`. Absolute, and ⛔ **not** tiered by seat.
- ⚠️ Scope-pinned card ⇒ AGENTS.md #11's opportunistic citation repair does **not** apply.

## Clause-②: `no` — measured

`PermissionMatrixEditor` is **absent** from `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`'s 25 named `metadata-admin` leaf re-exports (`:371`–`:428`); control — 84 `^export` lines on that entry. Adding a rejection handler inside a component body moves no signature. ⚠️ Re-measure at delivery and return `clause_2`. ⭐ And ⛔ do **not** report the mechanical floor `^\+export = 0` as if it were the answer — a sibling PR of mine this hour reported that floor as `0` when its own diff added **two** `^+export` lines. Count it from the diff you actually pushed.

## The pin

It must **fail on the pre-fix tree** and it must assert all three consequences, not just the strip. ⭐ The harness already exists and the card names it: `PermissionMatrixEditor.packageDoorRereadRefusal.test.tsx` (landed by PR objectui#9483) drives a client whose `layered` answers the published record for the load and rejects from the second call on, with **no `packageId`** — it observes `client.save` recording one body, i.e. the write landed, and then asserts the save and not the aftermath. Extend that reach rather than inventing a second harness.

⛔ The dirty-state consequence is the one most easily faked: assert it through whatever the component exposes as dirty / the unload guard, ⛔ not by reading a local variable.

## Serial constraints cleared

`packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/` — no open PR touches `metadata-admin`; I read all 9 changed-file lists this round. ⚠️ **Two siblings of mine are in this directory and I am naming both**: objectui#9464 is **in flight** on `metadata-admin/PermissionAdvancedFacets.tsx` (also a permission editor — ⛔ a different file, and ⛔ do not touch it), and PR objectui#9775 (card objectui#9382) is awaiting review on `metadata-admin/inspectors/datasetFilterCondition.ts`. Neither is your file. Merge `main` before opening your PR, and again if either lands while you are in flight; ⛔ never hand-order around them — the queue arbitrates.

## Return

The pre-fix red covering all three consequences, the `clause_2` field counted off your own diff, confirmation that `:437` and `:768` are untouched, and any premise of mine you falsified — ⭐ the card's own component name was already one. **A clean stop is a full success.**

## ⭐ THE FENCE HELD, and I measured it rather than accepting the claim

This was the one thing that could have gone badly, because triage's fence is that `:437`'s catch **blocks a write on purpose** and unifying the two doors would convert a deliberate guard into a degraded display — on a permission surface. Measured in my own act, branch head against `origin/main`:

| probe | main | head |

| ⭐ removed lines in the whole editor diff | — | **3**, and here they are: `setDraft(next);`, `const lay = await client.layered<…>(type, payload.name);`, `resetDraftBaseline(toDisplayDraft((lay.effective ?? toSave) …));` |

⇒ ✅ three removals, both fenced catches untouched, the two doors not unified. Exactly what the order required, and it is a reading rather than a promise.

## ⭐ The falsification that makes this PR worth more than its card

The card names three consequences and implies catching the rejection closes all three. **It does not, and nobody knew:**

> `isDirty` is a `useMemo` keyed on `draft` while its anchor lives in a ref; at environment scope the re-anchor falls back to the **saved body, which IS the current draft object**, so `setDraft` bailed out on `Object.is`, the memo never recomputed, and the editor went on reporting dirty against an anchor that already said clean.

⇒ the first version of the fix called `resetDraftBaseline` and the unload-guard assertion **still failed**. That is a measurement, not a theory, and it is the kind of thing a card written from reading the code path cannot see. ✅ The repair — `resetDraftBaseline` always handing `setDraft` a fresh shallow copy — is in the same file, the same defect class, mechanical, and adds no verification surface. ✅ Declared in the report, named in the PR body, and given **its own ablation leg**. That is an in-scope bounded repair properly handled, ⛔ not scope creep.

⚠️ Worth stating because it is the one thing a later reader should re-check: that copy changes `resetDraftBaseline` for **every** caller, including the load path and the package door. It is safe because it only bites where `next` is already `draft` — elsewhere the argument is freshly built — and because the anchor is a JSON snapshot, so a shallow copy is anchor-identical. ✅ The source comment says exactly that, in place.

## Two ablation legs, and the second one is the sharp one

✅ **Leg 1** — the editor file reverted to `origin/main`, proven on disk before any result was read (blob `88c94dad` vs HEAD `7048a337`, marker counts 2 → 0 and 1 → 0): `2 failed / 6 passed`, the failures naming **consequence 1** (`queryByText('layered read failed')` found a span — the red strip for a write that landed) and **consequence 3** (the `Destructive change` dialog heading). Both resolving-arm controls stayed green.

✅ **Leg 2** — only `setDraft({ ...next })` reverted to `setDraft(next)`, rejection handler left in place: `1 failed / 7 passed`, the failure being `expect(onDirtyChange).toHaveBeenLastCalledWith(false)` — **consequence 2**, under a strictly weaker mutation. ⭐ Leg 2 exists because leg 1 stops at consequence 1 and never reaches the dirty assertion. ⇒ each of the three consequences has its own pre-fix red. That is the shape I want and did not have to ask for.

Restore proven by the on-disk blob re-equalling `7048a337` **and** an empty `git diff HEAD` — ⛔ not by an exit code.

## The advisory notice — right call, and right reasoning

✅ The new state is separate from `error` on purpose, and the source says why: *"that strip means 'your save failed', which is the opposite of the truth here."* Amber, `role="status"`, cleared on set change and at the start of each save. One new designer-table key (`perm.save.rereadStale`, EN + ZH), with `check:i18n-designer-parity` and `check:i18n-drift` green and drift reporting **0 en values changed, 1 key added**.

## Clause-②: `no`

`PermissionMatrixEditor` is absent from the 25 named `metadata-admin` leaf re-exports on `packages/app-shell/src/index.ts`; no signature and no declarable key moves. ✅ `check-clause2-carriers.mjs --pair 9789` exits 0 — declaration readable in the fixed spelling, both carriers agree, no widening tell — and `needs:contract-review` is correctly **absent**. ✅ And the lane did **not** report `^\+export = 0` as the answer, which was the standing instruction after a sibling PR this hour reported that floor as `0` on a diff carrying two such lines.

## Carried out of review, correctly not filed

The load path's `stripReadDecorations` docblock still explains itself by saying `doSave`'s fresh read has a `.catch(() => null)` arm that *"falls back to this very body and spreads it into `client.save`"*. That arm became a **refusal** in objectui#9420, so the sentence's mechanism is historical — and this branch adds a `.catch(() => null)` on the **other** door whose fallback never reaches `client.save` at all, which makes the paragraph read as if it describes this change when it does not. ⚠️ Doc drift only; the call it justifies is still correct and still needed. ✅ Written into the PR's Acceptance notes for whoever next edits that call — the right home, since it is the docblock directly above the line they would be changing.
